description: I'm Isuru Lakmal Peiris, a founder and someone who is interested in creating things that haven't been built yet
summary:
Since May 2025, NASA's SPHEREx space telescope has mapped the entire sky every six months across 102 infrared wavelength channels (0.75 to 5.00 micrometers), capturing over one billion astronomical objects. Distant unknown solar system planets (Planet X), freezing brown dwarfs, comets, and variable stars reveal themselves by shifting position or changing brightness over time, but no science team or automated pipeline can inspect a billion 102-band objects alone.

SPHEREx x Planet X solves this discovery bottleneck with a zero-install, 60-FPS WebGL2 and WebAssembly platform that evolves the classic 2-band WiseView blink comparator into an interactive 4D spectrophotometric sky time machine (RA x Dec x 102 bands x N epochs). By bridging SPHEREx with 16 years of archival WISE/unWISE data (2010-2026), STScI MAST / ESA Gaia DR3 astrometry, and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) NEOSSat optical observations, our tool lets citizen scientists and researchers blink or subtract epochs in real time, subtract zodiacal light on GPU, inspect 102-band chemical spectra, and verify moving worlds live against five astronomical databases.

ONE-CLICK INTERACTIVE DEMO SCENARIOS

• Hunt WISE 0855-0714 (250 K Y4 Brown Dwarf / Planet X Analog): https://spherex-planetx-discovery-engine.vercel.app/?target=wise_0855&mode=1&fov=6

• Track Barnard's Star (10.39 arcsec/yr Fast Mover Dipole): https://spherex-planetx-discovery-engine.vercel.app/?target=barnards_star&mode=1&fov=6

• Awaken Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS (102-Band Coma CO2, H2O, CO): https://spherex-planetx-discovery-engine.vercel.app/?target=comet_3i_atlas_post&mode=2&fov=6

• Filter a Dusty Protostellar Outburst (WTP16aakapb QC Filter Demo): https://spherex-planetx-discovery-engine.vercel.app/?target=fuor_wtp16aakapb&mode=3&fov=6


1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Since May 2025, NASA's SPHEREx space telescope has photographed the entire sky every six months in 102 contiguous near-to-mid-infrared wavelength channels (0.75 to 5.00 micrometers), capturing over one billion objects. Moving solar system worlds (asteroids, comets, trans-Neptunian objects, and hypothesized Planet X), high-proper-motion brown dwarfs, and variable stars reveal themselves by shifting position or brightness across epochs.

While citizen-science tools like WiseView revolutionized 2-band broadband blinking for NASA's WISE mission, SPHEREx introduces a 51x higher spectral dimensionality, spatially varying Linear Variable Filter (LVF) bandpasses, bright zodiacal dust foregrounds (ZODI), and 32-bit hardware contamination flags (FLAGS).

SPHEREx x Planet X transforms SPHEREx Level-2 Multi-Extension FITS (MEF) cutouts into a real-time, 60-FPS WebGL2 and WebAssembly discovery workspace backed by a cloud FastAPI + DuckDB + Astropy scientific API. It synchronizes a 4D spectrophotometric hypercube (RA x Dec x 102 bands x N epochs) across a 16-year baseline (2010 to 2026) by bridging SPHEREx with archival unWISE coadds, STScI MAST / ESA Gaia DR3 proper-motion vectors, and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) NEOSSat optical observations.

2. HOW WE ADDRESSED ALL OFFICIAL CHALLENGE CONSIDERATIONS


• Pre-Validated on All 5 Official NASA Mandatory Test Targets: Includes instant toolbar buttons and dual-epoch coordinate aliases (J2000, 2010 WISE discovery, and 2025.8/2026.3 SPHEREx propagated coordinates) for Barnard's Star, WISE 0855-0714 (08h55m10.831s, -7d14m42.53s), Epsilon Indi Ba/Bb, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis, plus 13 additional benchmark discoveries (Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS, Luhman 16AB, WTP16aakapb, and the NEP persistence trap WISE J1833+6751).

• Easy Updates with Latest SPHEREx Releases: Dynamically queries Caltech/IPAC IRSA TAP tables (spherex.artifact and spherex.plane) across QR3 and QR2 collections and automatically adapts to FITS VERSION headers for both 3D PSF cubes and empirical EPSF binary tables.

• 6-Detector Array Co-Addition (4.1x SNR Boost) & Cold Object Filter: Provides a 1-click 6-Det SNR Co-Add button that stacks all 17 LVF sub-channels per detector array (D1 through D6) using inverse-variance weighting for a 4.1x signal-to-noise boost, alongside a D4-D2 Cold Object Filter (2.85 um minus 1.35 um) that highlights methane-absorbing Y-dwarfs and cold outer-solar-system bodies.

• On-the-Fly 102-Band Spectrophotometry (Extra Kudos): Extracts dual-epoch 102-band spectra across two physical regimes: Regime A performs point-source ePSF forced photometry with fit_ql quality filtering and L0-Y4 brown dwarf / SPLICES interstellar ice template matching; Regime B performs extended cometary coma profiling (Lisse et al. 2025/2026 modal annulus subtraction) to measure H2O, CO2, and CO gas production rates (Q_gas in molecules/s) on Comet 3I/ATLAS.

• Epoch Addition & Proper Image Subtraction: Implements 4 real-time WebGL2 GPU shader modes: Mode 0 (0.5 to 30 Hz Blink Comparator), Mode 1 (Lupton Color-Preserving Temporal Dipole RGB where stationary stars turn white and moving objects glow as Red-to-Blue pairs), Mode 2 (102-Band Spectral False-Color RGB), and Mode 3 (Fourier ZOGY Proper Image Subtraction split-curtain and S_corr significance heatmap).

• User-Selectable Field of View (FoV): Docked FoV selector (2'x2' Fast, 6'x6' Standard, 15'x15' Wide, and 30'x30' Sector Parallax) with automatic 6'x6' framing for fast movers so Barnard's Star (158.5 arcsec shift) and WISE 0855 (126.4 arcsec shift) never clip at the viewport edge.

• Multi-Mission Overlays & CSA NEOSSat Integration: Synchronizes Aladin Lite v3 (AllWISE IR, Pan-STARRS DR1 Optical disambiguation, DSS2, 2MASS, and SPHEREx HiPS) with our WebGL2 blink canvas, overlays Gaia DR3 proper-motion vectors, and integrates CSA NEOSSat CADC optical cutouts with a Joint NEOSSat+SPHEREx Near-Earth Asteroid Thermal Model (NEATM) solver to measure asteroid diameter, geometric albedo, and beaming parameters.

• Deep-Link URL Coordinate Querying & Website Embedding: Supports full URL query parameters (?ra=&dec=&fov=&mode=&band=&target=&embed=true) for one-click coordinate sharing and chromeless embedding into external citizen-science portals.

• Live Hardware Contamination (FLAGS) & Zodiacal Light (ZODI) Controls: Streams a 6-slice Float32 + Uint16 binary cube to the browser GPU. Slice 5 stores the modeled zodiacal dust foreground (ZODI) for sub-millisecond 60-FPS subtraction toggling, while the hardware bitmask hatches DICHROIC, NONFUNC, PERSIST, TRANSIENT, and SUR_ERROR pixels while preserving known reference catalog sources (MP_SOURCE Bit 21) and moving solar system outliers (MP_OUTLIER Bit 19).


3. INTENDED IMPACT, ACCESSIBILITY & CREATIVITY

• Built for Everyone (Interactive Plain-English Guide + Technical Specs): Includes a built-in Guide modal that explains SPHEREx, proper motion, and every panel in plain everyday English for students and citizen scientists alongside full mathematical specifications for astrophysicists, plus a dual-theme interface (Deep Space Dark Mode and Clean White Lab Mode).

• 5-API Live Verification & Zooniverse Citizen Science Export: Cross-checks any candidate in real time against Gaia DR3, CDS SIMBAD, IMCCE SkyBoT, JPL Horizons (sb_ident), and the Minor Planet Center (MPC), and exports uncatalogued discoveries to a Backyard Worlds / Zooniverse CSV in one click.


4. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & HARDWARE/SOFTWARE STACK

• Frontend (Hosted on Vercel): TypeScript, Next.js 14 (React 18), custom WebGL2 GLSL (#version 300 es) fragment shaders, Aladin Lite v3 (Rust/WASM HiPS engine), Apache ECharts, ONNX Runtime Web (WASM SIMD), and Tailwind CSS.

• Backend & Data Pipeline (Hosted on Hugging Face Spaces): Python 3.11+, FastAPI, DuckDB 1.2.1 (GeoParquet and spatial extensions), Astropy, reproject (reproject_exact), photutils, sep, SciPy, PyVO, Astroquery, aiohttp, PyTorch, and Docker.

5. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) & AI TOOLS


In compliance with NASA Space Apps Challenge SI guidelines:

• Code & Documentation Assistance: Generative AI / Large Language Model (SI) coding assistants were used to accelerate software architecture, TypeScript/React UI component implementation, GLSL shader optimization, cloud deployment configuration, and documentation editing. All astronomical calibration formulas, WCS reprojection pipelines, and API integrations were validated against official NASA/IPAC SPHEREx and CSA NEOSSat documentation.

• In-Browser Scientific Machine Learning: The client-side anomaly ranker (discoveryRanker.worker.ts) runs a transparent, open-source 290 KB INT8-quantized ONNX model ensemble (2D Convolutional Siamese Network + 1D Spectral Variational Autoencoder + 24-feature Isolation Forest) trained on synthetic SPHEREx PSF stamps to help users prioritize moving dipoles and spectral outliers.
